prompt.content:
You are analyzing the evaluation of one candidate change to a 3D-IC physical design flow.
Hypothesis of the change: The parent's best result came from giving the timing-driven placer broader net weighting (lilith) and a looser density-weight band; the untested complement is to make the GNN partition itself timing-aware by weighting positive (same-partition-desired) contrastive pairs by edge timing criticality, so timing-critical neighbors are pulled into the same embedding cluster and thus more likely onto the same tier (short, same-tier paths that rsz can repair with bottom-tier buffers).
Rule-based digest:
total=+0.590 robust(mean-std)=+0.181 min_case=+0.175 all_valid=True
  ariane133-ng45: score=+0.203 dWNS=+5.8% dTNS=+30.6% overflow~132
  bp-ng45: score=+0.212 dWNS=+10.3% dTNS=+28.1% overflow~120
  bp_fe-ng45: score=+0.175 dWNS=+21.3% dTNS=+14.9% overflow~105
Write <=120 words. If some runs are INVALID (failures listed), first say what kind of failure it is (legality / crash / timeout) and whether it looks systematic (all seeds of a case) or sporadic - an invalid candidate says nothing about the hypothesis itself; suggest how to make the same idea legal. Otherwise: (1) did the hypothesis hold? (2) which case/metric moved and plausible mechanism, (3) one concrete next-step suggestion. No preamble.

response: The hypothesis held: making the GNN partition timing-aware improved all three cases (total +0.590, robust +0.181, all valid). Gains concentrate in WNS/TNS: bp-ng45 dWNS +10.3%/dTNS +28.1%, bp_fe-ng45 dWNS +21.3%, ariane133-ng45 dTNS +30.6%, with overflow modest (~105–132). Mechanism is consistent—timing-critical neighbors co-clustered onto the same tier, yielding short same-tier paths repairable by bottom-tier buffers. Next step: sweep the criticality weighting exponent (and cap) to test whether stronger timing bias further improves WNS without inflating overflow, and verify on additional seeds.
